I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market. W: 对,牛肉。我打算为一个向国内市场供应牛肉的养牛场设计一个商业案例研究。 7 M: Well, that sounds very interesting and original. There's plenty of land out west. So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle. M: 当然了。非常有道理。西部有大量的土地。所以如果操作得当,自己养牛应该会很赚钱。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 10 W: Exactly. W: 没错。 11 M: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea. You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees. M: 说真的,这听起来是个很棒的主意。等我们拿到学位后,你真应该认真研究一下这个。 12 W: Thanks. So, your turn now. What are you doing your case study on? W: 谢谢。那现在轮到你了。你的案例研究做什么? 13 M: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea. M: 我想的是洗车行,但听了你这个绝妙的想法后,现在感觉我的主意好无聊。 14 W: That's cool. The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine. One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago. Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten. But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones? The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories and emotions are linked. 我们都知道嗅觉是强大的。例如,面包的香味可以像时光机一样发挥作用。一次嗅闻就能唤起多年前的记 忆。事实上,气味分子通常可以唤醒那些早已被遗忘的记忆。但为什么气味有时会引发强烈的记忆,尤其是 情感记忆呢?简单来说,是因为大脑中处理气味、记忆和情感的区域是相互关联的。 2 A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read. Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place. 气味是一种化学微粒,它通过鼻子飘入负责嗅觉的大脑区域,在那里感觉首先被处理成大脑可以读取的形 式。然后脑细胞将这些信息传递到处理情感的大脑区域,再传递到相邻的负责学习和记忆形成的大脑区域。 3 Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain. That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound. 气味是唯一以如此直接的路径传递到大脑情感和记忆中枢的感觉。这导致情感、记忆和气味之间形成了紧 密的联系,这就是为什么气味引发的记忆比视觉或听觉引发的记忆更具情感性。 4 Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated. Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation and then a memory might follow. But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface. Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past but won't remember what they experienced. What causes this baffling phenomenon? The explanation is context. Imagine this scenario—a person is walking down the street smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response. If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory. 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。通常,当一个人闻到与他们过去某个有意义的事件相关的气 味时,他们首先会对这种感觉产生情感反应,然后可能会跟随一段记忆。但有时,记忆并不会浮现出来。这个 人可能会感受到过去发生的某件事的情感,但不会记得他们经历了什么。是什么导致了这种令人困惑的现 象?答案是情境。想象这样一个场景——一个人走在街上,闻到了几十年前第一次遇到的气味,这激活了情感 反应。如果这个人第一次遇到这种气味时处于完全不同的情境中,那么恢复相关记忆将会困难得多,因为大 脑使用情境来赋予信息意义并找到那段记忆。 5 The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories. They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time. In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted. But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't. 尽管气味唤回的记忆具有特殊性,但它们也有与其他记忆相同的缺陷。它们并不总是准确的,而且会随时间 变化。事实上,每次我们记起某件事时,那段记忆都可能被扭曲。但是,由于这些记忆唤起的强烈情感联系,因 气味而记起某事的人往往确信记忆是准确的,即使它们并非如此。

analysis.text: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 问作者对乡村生活方式的明确观点， 答案是原文直接写出的评价，并未要求做逻辑推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 是固定句型，think of=「对……的看 法」；直译「作者怎么看乡村生活方式」，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice. 我们在城市里也许像盒子一样堆在一起，但这带来了乡村无法企及的能效。乡村的能耗导致 人均碳排比城市更高，因此推崇这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。 47. What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? A) It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes. B) It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities. C) It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles. D) It is a choice more affluent people will endorse.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 P3 评价乡村生活方式不可取，但并未说它「无法存活」；It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes. 借用了 how can the countryside ensure its survival 里的 survival，却把「能否生存」的话题误植到「作者对生活方式的判断」上。 B) ✓ 正确 this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match ↔ It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities. higher carbon emissions per person than in the city ↔ It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities. 整段评价的核心证据就是「乡村能效低、碳排高」，B 一字不差地复述了这层比较关 系，且严格限定在「能效」维度，与预判一致。 C) 偷换概念 those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users 说的是「乡村人是更 重度的汽车使用者」（使用频率/比例更高），选项 It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles. 把 heavier 移植到 automobiles 之前，变成「依赖重型汽车」， 偷换了 heavier 的修饰对象。 D) 与原文相反 原文 it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice 直接评价「推崇这 种生活方式是不负责任的」，作者持反对态度；选项 It is a choice more affluent people will endorse. 不仅没指出作者的反对，反而把「有钱人会推崇」当成结论。 作者如何看待富裕的城市居民在农村购买第二套住房? A) 这必然会破坏传统的农村生活。 B) 这对农村社会稳定产生不利影响。 C) 这阻碍了农村经济的复兴。 D) 这不利于农村保护。

options.label: A
options.text: It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes.

options.label: B
options.text: It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.

options.label: C
options.text: It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a choice more affluent people will endorse.

questions.stem: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside? 问的是作者对这一具体行为的明确评价，答案出现在原文同一段的总结句。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside 中 buying 是现在分词 作 residents 的后置定语，相当于「买第二套乡村房的城市富人」；定语稍长但不绕。 48. What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside? A) It is bound to mar the traditional rural life. B) It adversely impacts rural social stability. C) It hinders rural economies' revitalisation. D) It is detrimental to rural preservation.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable. 这一难题尚无解决方案，因为市场力量正在进一步把居民赶出乡村。对那些信奉乡村保护的 人而言，这是令人痛心的。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 P4 谈的是房价与本地居民问题，并未提及 traditional rural life 是否被破坏；考生易把 第二段提到的「亲密社区/简单生活」的传统印象嫁接到此，但原文未在 P4 谈这一面。 B) 偷换概念 原文 house prices are pushed up... leaving them unaffordable for local people 谈 的是房价与可负担性，并未谈 rural social stability；选项把经济层面问题升格成「社会 稳定」这种更大的范畴。 C) 无中生有 P4 谈的是市场力量与房价，并未提及 rural economies' revitalisation；revitalisation 这一话题在 P6 rural renaissance 处才隐约出现，与 P4 的论点无关。 D) ✓ 正确 For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable ↔ It is detrimental to rural preservation. leaving them unaffordable for local people ↔It is detrimental to rural preservation. 原文连续给出「房价上涨 本地人买不起 市场力量进一步驱赶居民 对乡村保护者而 言可悲」四步推理，落脚点正是「对乡村保护不利」；D 既保留了评价的负面性，又精 准落到 preservation 这个对象上。 关于伴随工业化和技术进步的农村,我们了解到什么? A) 它注定会逐渐改变。 B) 它将呈现一种理想化的生活方式。 C) 它有可能接纳外来文化。 D) 它将变得日益多元化。

options.label: A
options.text: It is bound to mar the traditional rural life.

options.label: B
options.text: It adversely impacts rural social stability.

options.label: D
options.text: It is detrimental to rural preservation.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances? 问从文中得知什么，答案直接来自原文表述，不要求二步推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances 中 with 引出伴随状 语，意为「在工业化与技术进步的影响下」，with 短语作 countryside 的后置修饰，整句 直译「在工业化与技术进步下，我们对乡村得知什么」。 49. What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances? A) It is destined to change gradually. B) It will present an idealised way of life. C) It is likely to embrace foreign cultures. D) It will become increasingly diversified.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable. 尽管对乡村理想化的印象很常见，现实却是乡村生活一直在持续演变。工业化带来分工增 加，改变了乡村人之间的社会联系。互联网把曾经陌生的文化带进了乡村。交通改善与可承 受让世界更触手可及，造就了「地球村」。鉴于这些变化，乡村必然在演变之中。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 surely an evolving countryside is inevitable ↔It is destined to change gradually. rural life has continuously evolved ↔It is destined to change gradually. P5 段尾既明示必然性（inevitable）又通过 continuously evolved 暗示渐进性，A 把 这两层语义都包含进 destined to change gradually，与预判完全一致。 B) 与原文相反 原文 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved 用 whilst 让步、the reality is 转折，明确把「理 想化乡村」当成被否定的印象；选项 It will present an idealised way of life. 反把它说 成将要呈现的现实。 C) 以偏概全 The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside 只是段中 三件平行例证之一，与「分工」「全球村」共同支撑「乡村必然演变」这一论点；选项 It is likely to embrace foreign cultures. 把单一例子当成结论。 D) 过度推断 creating a "global village" 强调「世界更可及、变成地球村」，并不等于乡村会「越来 越多元化」；选项 It will become increasingly diversified. 在「多文化进入」之上多走 一步，推出 diversified 这个原文未说的结论。 作者如何看待农村与城市相比的未来? A) 对于当地人来说,情况会更加艰难。 B) 它将与城市的未来相似。 C) 它不太可能保持静止不变。 D) 它更不容易设想。

options.label: A
options.text: It is destined to change gradually.

options.label: B
options.text: It will present an idealised way of life.

options.label: C
options.text: It is likely to embrace foreign cultures.

questions.stem: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 问作者对未来的对比判断，原文末段直接给出明示对比，不需推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 中 compared with cities 是过去分词短语作 future 的后置定语，意为「与城市相比的乡村 的未来」；句子结构稍长但语义直白。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear. 我们知道，世界将看到新城从尘土中崛起、现有城市发展为超大型城市，但乡村的未来则不 那么清晰。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 P7 未提及 harder for the locals；本地人变难的话题在 P4 leaving them unaffordable for local people 出现过，但与「未来对比」无关；选项把跨段细节挪过 来冒充末段对比的结论。 B) 与原文相反 原文 but the future of the countryside is less clear 把乡村未来与城市未来拉开差 距；选项 It is going to resemble that of cities. 反说「乡村未来会像城市的未来」，把 对比关系反转为类似关系。 C) 答非所问 But change is inevitable 谈的是变化必然，It is less likely to stay static. 复述这一变 化必然性；但本题问的是「乡村未来与城市未来相比」这一对比维度，C 答的是「乡村 是否会变」的另一维度。 D) ✓ 正确 but the future of the countryside is less clear ↔It is less easy to envisage. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities ↔It is less easy to envisage. 对比型细节题正确项必须同时保留比较关系与比较内容；D 既保留 less，又把 clear 同 义置换为 easy to envisage，与预判完全契合。

options.label: A
options.text: It is going to be harder for the locals.

options.label: B
options.text: It is going to resemble that of cities.

options.label: C
options.text: It is less likely to stay static.

options.label: D
options.text: It is less easy to envisage.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干 What does the passage say about the statement 把范围圈死在那句引语上，要求 复述作者对它的具体描述，不是推断也不是主旨。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"? 主干是 What does the passage say about X，X = the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"；structure 平铺直叙，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. 诸如「美在观看者的眼中」这样的说法，几乎从不受到质疑。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 rarely questioned ↔hardly ever been disputed 预判「几乎无人质疑」与 hardly ever been disputed 在频率与语义上完全等值，锁 定 A。 B) 偷换概念 It can be interpreted aesthetically 说「它可被审美地解读」，与原文 rarely questioned 完全无关；作者只说「无人质疑」，没说「可被审美解读」。 C) 与原文相反 原文说「人们觉得 absurd to think otherwise」（反着想才荒谬），而 Many people have found it absurd 把「荒谬」直接扣给那句谚语本身，正话反说。 D) 无中生有 People have long been misled by it 说「人们长期被它误导」，原文只说作者「想 push back 一下」，并未给该谚语贴「误导」标签。 51. What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"? A) It has hardly ever been disputed. B) It can be interpreted aesthetically. C) Many people have found it absurd. D) People have long been misled by it. 最近一项探索审美品味的研究显示了什么? A) 审美品味往往因人而异。 B) 自然美很少被人工美所超越。 C) 人们对人工制品的共识较少。 D) 人们对什么是赏心悦目的存在普遍共识。

options.label: A
options.text: It has hardly ever been disputed.

options.label: C
options.text: Many people have found it absurd.

options.label: D
options.text: People have long been misled by it.

questions.stem: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show 问的是一项具体研究 show 出什么——属于事实复述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show? 主干是 What does a study show；exploring aesthetic taste 是 study 的现在分词后置定语，作用是限定哪项研究。 结构清晰，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects. 这项研究的结果显示，人们对自然物的审美评价高度一致，但对人造物（即人工制造的物 品）则分歧更多。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 以偏概全 Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person 把原文「人造物上分歧」扩大 成「审美口味本来就因人而异」，丢掉了原文「自然物上一致」这一半。 B) 偷换概念 Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty 把研究讲成「自然美几乎不被 人造美超越」，原文谈的是「评价一致性」，不是「美的优劣比较」。 C) ✓ 正确 they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects ↔ less consensus on objects shaped by human craft 预判要求选项聚焦「人造物上分歧更多」，less consensus on objects shaped by human craft 完整对应该语义，锁 C。 D) 以偏概全 There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye 只说「人们对什么好看 普遍一致」，丢掉了原文「对人造物分歧更多」这关键一半，与研究的对比结论不符。 52. What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show? A) Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person. B) Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty. C) There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft. D) There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye. 为什么人们对人工制品的审美评价存在差异? A) 它们的设计种类繁多。 B) 它们导致不同的行为后果。 C) 它们占用的自然空间比风景少得多。 D) 它们进入人们视野的频率低于自然空间。

options.label: A
options.text: Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person.

options.label: B
options.text: Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty.

options.label: C
options.text: There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft.

options.label: D
options.text: There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye.

questions.stem: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts 问的是一项已写明的具体 原因，不是让你推断作者的言外之意。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? 一般疑问句结构 Why do S V O，differ in 是固定搭配（在某方面有差异）；无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste. 艺术与建筑（不像自然空间）没有同等程度的曝光度。因此，人们对它们的共同审美趣味也 达不到同样的程度。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 They come out in a great variety of designs 谈的是「设计多样」，与原文给出的原 因 exposure 完全无关；这是 P9 里 a wide array of embodiments 的话被移花接木 过来。 B) 与原文相反 P6 明说差异 has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences"——作者用 rather than 否定了 behavioral consequences；They lead to varying behavioral consequences 反而把被否定的那一支抬回来当原因。 C) 无中生有 They take up much less natural space than landscapes 说人造物比自然景观「占 用的自然空间更少」，原文从未做过这种空间面积比较；这是按生活常识替原文补造的 对比。 D) ✓ 正确 do not have the same level of exposure ↔ come into people's view less often than natural spaces 预判要求「人造物被看到的机会少」，与 come into people's view less often than natural spaces 完全等值，锁 D。 53. Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? A) They come out in a great variety of designs. B) They lead to varying behavioral consequences. C) They take up much less natural space than landscapes. D) They come into people's view less often than natural spaces. 日落的例子说明了自然的什么特点? A) 它通过灿烂的光辉产生强大的吸引力。 B) 它在世界各地以相似的方式展现美学特征。 C) 它以广泛的美学特征体现美。 D) 它以多种方式确立了美的原则。

options.label: A
options.text: They come out in a great variety of designs.

options.label: B
options.text: They lead to varying behavioral consequences.

options.label: C
options.text: They take up much less natural space than landscapes.

options.label: D
options.text: They come into people's view less often than natural spaces.

questions.stem: What does the example of sunset tell about nature?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the example of sunset tell about nature 问的是举这个例子是为了告诉读者 关于 nature 的什么——典型的「例证目的」考法。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the example of sunset tell about nature? 主干 What does X tell about Y； tell 在此处意为 reveal / indicate（说明、揭示），不要按字面理解为「告诉某人某事」。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal. 自然界以共通的方式在世界各地呈现某些普遍的审美特征（比如光辉）。各处并不完全相 同，但确实有共通之处。例如，落日在不同地方足够相似，因而几乎能引起普世的吸引力。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance 谈的是「落日靠光辉本身 创造强烈吸引力」，是 sunset 例子的表层描写，不是例子要说明的论点（共通性）。 B) ✓ 正确 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world ↔It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over 预判要求「自然在全球以共通方式呈现审美特征」，It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over 与论点句逐项匹配，锁 B。 C) 张冠李戴 It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features 借用 a wide array of embodiments 与 Possible universal principles of beauty 的短语，但 P9 谈的是「美 的原则允许多样体现」，不是 sunset 例子要说明的内容。 D) 过度推断 It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways 把「sunset 例证一种共 通呈现方式」夸大成「确立了多个美学原则」，原文从未把 sunset 提到「确立原则」的 高度。 54. What does the example of sunset tell about nature? A) It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance. B) It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over. C) It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features. D) It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways. 为什么人工制品并不总是具有普遍吸引力? A) 对其美的欣赏不受客观标准的约束。 B) 美的普遍原则阻止了广泛的体现方式。 C) 其创作者应用美的原则的方式可能无法取悦所有人。 D) 其创作者各自以自己偏好的方式诠释美的普遍原则。

options.label: A
options.text: It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance.

options.label: B
options.text: It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over.

options.label: C
options.text: It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features.

options.label: D
options.text: It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways.

questions.stem: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal 仍是对已写明原因的复述问法，作者 已经直接写出「为什么」，不是推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal? 否定副词 not always 表示「并非总 是」（部分否定），不是「从来不」；不要错读成 never。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal. 当人们投身于建筑或艺术中的人造物创作时，他们以独特的方式运用这些非常宽泛的概念。 但他们运用原则的方式未必能引起所有人的共鸣。

analysis.label: 选项

A) Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.
B) The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
C) Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
D) Look, it's okay if you don't know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.
E) The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
F) The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee(近地点), and the most distant point is apogee(远地点). 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
G) The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
H) Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
I) A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
J) In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
K) Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue". Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
L) You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
M) Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical. N) Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so. 36. We cannot see the moon at times when it is positioned right between the earth and the sun.

P1 With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.

P2 Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.

P3 So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes; or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.

P4 Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.

P5 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.

P6 Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?

P7 As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.

reading-2.raw:
P1 Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.

P2 A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects. 

P3 The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.

P4 Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.

P5 Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.

P6 It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".

P7 All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.

P8 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.

P9 Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.

P10 This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.

blocks.text: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.

blocks.label: P3
blocks.text: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.

blocks.label: P4
blocks.text: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.

blocks.label: P5
blocks.text: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.

blocks.label: P6
blocks.text: It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".

blocks.label: P7
blocks.text: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.

blocks.label: P8
blocks.text: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.

blocks.label: P9
blocks.text: Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.

blocks.label: P10
blocks.text: This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.

blocks.label: P11
blocks.text: 明说差异 has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences"——作者用 rather than 否定了 behavioral consequences；They C) They take up much less natural space than landscapes 说人造物比自然景观「占 D) do not have the same level of exposure ↔ come into people's view less often than natural spaces 53. Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? A) They come out in a great variety of designs. B) They lead to varying behavioral consequences. C) They take up much less natural space than landscapes. D) They come into people's view less often than natural spaces.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
writing.model: Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth. In an age flooded with short videos and endless distractions, the ability to control oneself has become the very foundation of academic success and character building. A vivid example is my roommate Li Ming. When we entered university, he set himself a firm rule: no phone before finishing the day's study plan. While others drifted from one game to another, his steady self- management allowed him to master a difficult programming course and win a national scholarship. His experience convinced me that talent alone rarely decides how far a person goes; it is perseverance and daily self-control that truly shape our future. Therefore, I firmly believe that cultivating self-discipline deserves our full attention. Rather than blaming the environment for our failures, we should learn to say no to temptations and stick to our own plans. Only by mastering ourselves can we grow into the people we truly wish to become.

translation.reference: Yangshan Port is an important part of the Shanghai shipping center, China's first deep-water port, and one of the largest deep-water ports in the world. After nearly two decades of development, it has achieved a high level of automation. The use of digital technology and artificial intelligence has greatly reduced labor costs and carbon emissions. The self-developed terminal management system can remotely control large equipment from hundreds of kilometers away. The port looks busy, but no manual operation can be seen on site, and it can operate around the clock without interruption. Yangshan Port will continue to develop and make greater contributions to building Shanghai into a global shipping center.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 洋山港 is 三个并列表语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 洋山港,谓语是三个并列的判断"是…,是…,也是…"。英文主干立成 Yangshan Port is...，主语 Yangshan Port,系动词 is,后接三个并列的表语成分,不必拆成三个完整句子重复 主语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三个表语并列降级 把后两个"是…"降级为与第一个表语并列的名词短语,共用一个 is:重要组成部分→an important part of...,中国第一个深水港→China's first deep-water port,世界上规模最大的深水港之一→one of the largest deep-water ports in the world,三者用逗号加 and 串联,避免照中文重复三遍 it is。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时 is——陈述洋山港现在的地位这一事实。 单复数 世界上规模最大的深水港之一的"之一"意味着同类有多个,one of 后必须接复数 deep-water ports, 主体考生常误写成单数 port。 冠词 "重要组成部分"是泛指其中一个,用不定冠词 an important part;"第一个深水港"有序数词"第一",可 用所有格 China's first... 或定冠词,但 China's 已限定,不再加 the。
